newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn said not to continue income tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn said not to continue income tax cuts.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told the National Assembly's finance committee on Wednesday the previous government's income tax cut plan would not be continued, according to minutes released on Thursday.

The minutes of the closed-door session said he had told the committee that nothing had been decided in terms of 1998 tax measures "but that the programme of income tax cuts drawn up by the previous government would not be continued, the priority being to reduce VAT once public finances permitted".
The previous government had adopted a five-year plan for income tax cuts worth a total 25 billion, with the first 25 billion francs worth of cuts in 1997.
Strauss-Kahn made it clear at a news conference on Thursday morning that the previous centre-right government's income tax cut plan was in the firing line.
He told reporters cutting value-added tax was the priority.

He also said that if the public deficit in France turned out bigger than expected, this would prove the strategy of income tax cuts was a policy that had been drawn up without the necessary resources.
